questions.answer: $\int \frac{1}{ax+b} dx = \frac{1}{a}\ln|ax+b| + C$. Multiplying by 2 gives $\frac{2}{3}\ln|3x - 1| + C$.
Let $u = x^2 + 1, du = 2x dx$. Integral from $u = 1$ to $u = 2$: $\int_1^2 \frac{1}{2u} du = [\frac{1}{2}\ln u]_1^2 = \frac{1}{2}\ln 2$.

questions.q: Use the substitution $x = 2\sin\theta$ to find $\int \sqrt{4 - x^2}\,dx$.

questions.answer: Let $u = x, dv = e^{3x} dx \Rightarrow du = dx, v = \frac{1}{3}e^{3x}$. $uv - \int v du = \frac{1}{3}x e^{3x} - \int \frac{1}{3}e^{3x} dx = \frac{x e^{3x}}{3} - \frac{e^{3x}}{9} + C$.

$u = \ln x, dv = x dx \Rightarrow du = dx/x, v = x^2/2$. $[\frac{x^2}{2}\ln x]_1^e - \int_1^e \frac{x}{2} dx = \frac{e^2}{2} - [\frac{x^2}{4}]_1^e = \frac{e^2}{2} - (\frac{e^2}{4} - \frac{1}{4}) = \frac{e^2 + 1}{4}$.
$u = x, dv = \sin x dx \Rightarrow du = dx, v = -\cos x$. $[-x\cos x]_0^\pi - \int_0^\pi (-\cos x) dx = -\pi(-1) - 0 + [\sin x]_0^\pi = \pi + 0 = \pi$.

sections.heading: Section 4: Partial Fractions Integration & Trapezium Rule

questions.q: Use the trapezium rule with 4 intervals (5 ordinates) to approximate $\int_1^3 \dfrac{1}{x}\,dx$.
Is the trapezium rule approximation in the previous question an overestimate or underestimate, and why?
choices: Overestimate, because the curve $y = 1/x$ is concave up
Overestimate, because the intervals are too wide
Underestimate, because the chords lie below the curve
questions.answer: Since $d^2y/dx^2 = 2/x^3 > 0$ for $x > 0$, the curve is convex (concave up). The straight line chords lie above the curve, producing an overestimate.
